question.text:
A computer system features a two-level cache. The L1 cache has an access time of $10$ ns and a hit rate of $90 \%$. The L2 cache has an access time of $40$ ns and a local hit rate of $95 \%$ (for misses from L1). The main memory has an access time of $200$ ns. What is the average memory access time (AMAT) for this system?

  1. $15$ ns
     
  2. $34$ ns
     
  3. $13.8$ ns
     
  4. $50$ ns
question.subject: CO & Architecture

question.text:
A four-way set associative cache memory unit with a capacity of $32$ KB is built using a block size of $16$ words. The word length is $32$ bits. The physical address space is $4$ GB . The number of bits in the TAG, SET fields are

  1. $19,7$
     
  2. $17,9$
     
  3. $21,7$
     
  4. $19,8$
question.subject: CO & Architecture

question.text:
A particular parallel program computation requires $100$ sec when executed on a single processor. If $40 \%$ of this computation is inherently sequential (i.e., will not benefit from additional processors), then theoretically best possible elapsed times of this program running with 2 and 4 processors, respectively, are

  1. $20$ sec and $10$ sec
     
  2. $30$ sec and $15$ sec
     
  3. $50$ sec and $25$ sec
     
  4. $70$ sec and $55$ sec
question.subject: CO & Architecture

question.text:
A machine has a $32$-bit architecture with $1$-word-long instructions. It has $64$ registers, each of which is $32$ bits long. It needs to support $45$ instructions, which have an immediate operand in addition to two register operands. Assuming that the immediate operand is an unsigned integer, the maximum value of the immediate operand is

  1. $16383$
     
  2. $32767$
     
  3. $65535$
     
  4. $131071$
question.subject: CO & Architecture

question.text:
A byte addressable computer has a memory capacity of $2^m \mathrm{~KB}$ (kbytes) and can perform $2^n$ operations. An instruction involving 3 operands and one operator needs maximum of

  1. $3m$ bits
     
  2. $3 m+n$ bits
     
  3. $m+n$ bits
     
  4. None of the above
question.subject: CO & Architecture
